chapters.title: Chapter 778: Two Fierce Kittens [Bonus ]
paragraphs: No swords, at least. Just bare fists and many bad ideas.
Natalie blinked. “Is... is that okay? They seem to be very angry and hurt!”

Sylvaris sighed, resting her forehead against the window frame. “Those two get along like oil and water. If we’re lucky, they’ll only bruise each other. If we’re unlucky, they’ll level a building or so...”
Another thump followed as Ayame managed to tackle Iris into a barrel, shattering it into splinters. A loud squawk from a terrified chicken echoed somewhere nearby.

Natalie couldn’t help it. The sight of these two was just too ridiculous for a woman who had spent her last two decades living in a forest and the last few months in chains. As such, she sputtered by instinct, after which she swiftly moved her hands, covering her mouth to avoid laughing.
“Should we... stop them?” she asked.

“If they keep it up, we won’t have a choice. I can’t let them destroy what the hard-working laborers had just finished building through painstaking effort.” Sylvaris had a rather exhausted expression, letting the dogkin woman know this serene elf didn’t appreciate having her tea time interrupted.

Ayame and Iris writhed on the ground like a pair of feral cats. Dirt was kicking up in large amounts as they rolled, swinging their fists wildly at each other. Every strike of theirs was paired with a sharp insult, making their snarling voices echo through the courtyard.

“Who’s a flat chested female goblin, you emo bitch?!” Ayame shouted, pinning Iris for half a second before springing back, mock tears glistening in her eyes as she clutched at her heart dramatically. In a mocking, high-pitched wail, she mimicked Iris’s tone to the best of her ability.
“Oh, I’m so sad and lonely, Quinlan! I’m here, alone, in the corner... When will you notice me? When will you console me? I’m so pitiful... Will you cheer me up?”

Iris’ face flushed red with fury. “I’ve never once begged for his attention! Your unhinged brain is making up fantasies so that you can cope instead of admitting you’re one jealous cunt because he’s chasing after me instead of you, knowing you’ll part your legs as soon as he asks!”
Ayame’s eye twitched at a speed that wouldn’t be perceivable for the average human eye.

The two feral kittens somehow managed to stand on their two feet, and Iris instantly lunged, slugging Ayame in the shoulder. The impact of the hit jerked the samurai’s body to the side, forcing a grimace from her lips.
But just as Iris moved in to follow up, ready to land another blow, Ayame’s footwork turned lightning-quick.

With a sharp breath, Ayame vanished in a blur, reappearing behind Iris in a single flicker of motion. Her hands gripped onto Iris’ long, black hair, and with a wild scream, she hurled the Child of Reckoning into the air like a missile launched for the heavens.

Iris soared through the skies with her expression caught between fury and disbelief, not expecting the samurai to speed-blitz her in this fashion. For the longest time, she was slightly stronger than Ayame due to her higher level and simply superior class, but... As much as it pained the woman to admit, the XP boost from Quinlan’s [Blessed Seed] and the Skysplitter class from Rosie’s gift made Ayame into an incredibly formidable fighter.
Just as Iris reached the apex of her flight. Ayame bent her knees.
And then she launched, rocketing toward Iris like a guided arrow.

In the skies above the stronghold, the battle erupted into a ballet of chaos. Iris twisted mid-air, but Ayame was faster than she expected. The oriental beauty twirled her lithe body, making her heel slam into Iris’ side with a crack of her ribs that echoed across the rooftops. Iris retaliated while biting her lip as she flung her fists like a tiny comet, the shockwave enough to slow Ayame’s pursuit and give her room to recover.
Below, the courtyard had descended into confused chaos, and at its front, barreling through the garden like a pink rocket, came Rosie.
“Mommy and Aunty are fighting!!” she squealed, zooming around so fast she looked like an overgrown, green, sugar-high bee on steroids.
“Go, Mommy, go! The Elysiars never lose!”

As the aerial brawl raged above, all anyone below could do was gawk, until finally, with a burst of displaced air, Iris and Ayame came crashing down, landing in twin crouches like lightning bolts slamming into earth.
The instant their feet hit the ground, Ayame surged forward, but then, an arm suddenly wrapped around her waist, yanking her into the air like she weighed nothing.
“Enough.”
Lucille.
The ex-Berserker, now Bloodmonger, had a grip that was unyielding. Ayame flailed with her legs kicking at the ground.
“Let go of me, you damn ogre! She started it!”
“Did she now?” Lucille mused as her hold only grew tighter.
Despite all her technique and finesse, Ayame was no match for her raw brute force. She squirmed, twisted, even tried a clever shoulder dislocation to escape the hold, but Lucille didn’t budge.
Across from them, Iris cracked her knuckles, but before she could charge at her rival once again, four figures crashed into her from the side like members of a rugby team.
“Get her arms! Grab her legs!” Seraphiel grunted, using her Dawnbringer strength to try and keep one of Iris’ limbs pinned.
Lyra wrapped her arms around Iris’ midsection, but the woman still bucked and twisted like a captured wild beast.
Blossom, the calmest of the squad, gritted her teeth as she straddled Iris’ upper body and did her best to keep the woman pinned to the ground.
In the meantime, Poppy accepted the most dangerous job of the bunch, which was somehow trying to restrain Iris’s hands.
She didn’t have a resounding success.
“She’s strong—!!” Lyra gasped.
“Blossom is not built for this...!” Blossom murmured with difficulty. Her Agility-focused build was making her job very troublesome.
“Neither am I!!!” Poppy cried after getting punched in her palm.
“What is she, a bull?! Also, I’ll heal you as soon as I get the chance, so hang in there!” Seraphiel grunted as even the four of them struggled to restrain her properly.
From a safe distance, Aurora watched with an amused as she sipped from a teacup.
“If Quin were here, he’d have grabbed a bag of popcorn and watched this ‘kitten fight,’ as he would call it, with sparkling eyes,” she mused.
At that moment, Rosie zipped over, buzzing with excitement. “Big sis Aurora, big sis Aurora! Why aren’t you joining in?! It looks fun! If only Rosie were bigger and stronger!”

Aurora smiled smugly. “Because, unlike Seraphiel, I didn’t gain a class that boosts my physical stats. One wild elbow from either of them and I’d be red paste on the floor. So—” she took another dainty sip, “—it can’t be helped.”
Rosie stared at her blankly.
“Big sis Aurora is boring!!” she declared with child-like conviction, then zoomed away like a sugar-powered missile, heading straight toward the chaos again.
Lucille, still holding Ayame in a tight lock, looked up at her approach with a deadpan expression.
“Someone catch the overly energetic green bee,” she muttered.
Amidst the spiraling madness, laughter started bubbling from Natalie, who had long since abandoned any attempts to appear composed.
She chuckled, wiping a tear from her eye, “It seems this place never gets boring.”
Sylvaris simply sighed with her eyes closed from mental exhaustion.
“... You have no idea.”
While the ladies were having fun, Quinlan was busy testing his necromantic abilities!

If we’re lucky, they’ll only bruise each other.
If we’re unlucky, they’ll level a building or so...”
Another thump followed as Ayame managed to tackle Iris into a barrel, shattering it into splinters.
A loud squawk from a terrified chicken echoed somewhere nearby.
Natalie couldn’t help it.
The sight of these two was just too ridiculous for a woman who had spent her last two decades living in a forest and the last few months in chains.

“If they keep it up, we won’t have a choice.

I can’t let them destroy what the hard-working laborers had just finished building through painstaking effort.” Sylvaris had a rather exhausted expression, letting the dogkin woman know this serene elf didn’t appreciate having her tea time interrupted.
Ayame and Iris writhed on the ground like a pair of feral cats.
Dirt was kicking up in large amounts as they rolled, swinging their fists wildly at each other.
Every strike of theirs was paired with a sharp insult, making their snarling voices echo through the courtyard.

I’m here, alone, in the corner...

When will you console me?
I’m so pitiful...
Will you cheer me up?”
Iris’ face flushed red with fury.
“I’ve never once begged for his attention!

Your unhinged brain is making up fantasies so that you can cope instead of admitting you’re one jealous cunt because he’s chasing after me instead of you, knowing you’ll part your legs as soon as he asks!”
Ayame’s eye twitched at a speed that wouldn’t be perceivable for the average human eye.

The impact of the hit jerked the samurai’s body to the side, forcing a grimace from her lips.
But just as Iris moved in to follow up, ready to land another blow, Ayame’s footwork turned lightning-quick.
With a sharp breath, Ayame vanished in a blur, reappearing behind Iris in a single flicker of motion.
Her hands gripped onto Iris’ long, black hair, and with a wild scream, she hurled the Child of Reckoning into the air like a missile launched for the heavens.
Iris soared through the skies with her expression caught between fury and disbelief, not expecting the samurai to speed-blitz her in this fashion.
For the longest time, she was slightly stronger than Ayame due to her higher level and simply superior class, but...
As much as it pained the woman to admit, the XP boost from Quinlan’s [Blessed Seed] and the Skysplitter class from Rosie’s gift made Ayame into an incredibly formidable fighter.
Just as Iris reached the apex of her flight.
Ayame bent her knees.
And then she launched, rocketing toward Iris like a guided arrow.
In the skies above the stronghold, the battle erupted into a ballet of chaos.
Iris twisted mid-air, but Ayame was faster than she expected.
The oriental beauty twirled her lithe body, making her heel slam into Iris’ side with a crack of her ribs that echoed across the rooftops.
Iris retaliated while biting her lip as she flung her fists like a tiny comet, the shockwave enough to slow Ayame’s pursuit and give her room to recover.

“Go, Mommy, go!
The Elysiars never lose!”

Lucille.

chapters.title: Chapter 779: Uncovering the Secrets of Necromancy
paragraphs: – PoV: Quinlan –
I stretched out on the fresh mattress, the one we’d swapped in to replace the old one that was now fully stained with sweat and... other evidence of our hard labor.

Vex lay curled against my left side with her warm purrs vibrating through my chest like a soft engine. My right hand propped my head up, elbow buried in the pillow, while my left arm wrapped around her, palm resting possessively on her sensual butt.

She nuzzled in closer, resting her head on my shoulder, and one hand of hers began drifting down to cup and gently massage my balls. It felt as if it was meant to be a tender apology for the brutal “duel” she’d demanded from my twin jewels. Each careful squeeze made me sigh in pleasure and pure happiness.
I felt greatly fulfilled right now.

Now that I was in great safety, and the afterglow of a most successful and pleasurable day, I allowed my mind to drift back to something of great importance: It was more than fine to lie with my women, but I couldn’t afford to lose myself in hedonistic pleasure forever. I had to master these new necromantic powers.
Here, there would be no more rushed glimpses in the middle of battle as it was when I desperately searched for ways to slow the Sunfang down back in Lionheart.
It was time to lock in.
I whispered the summoning call under my breath:
“[Necromantic Codex].”

With a slow shimmer, the ancient tome materialized. It hovered inches from my face with its pages fluttering as if caught in an unseen breeze. Perfect. I didn’t need to free a single finger to read it: the book remained suspended in the air, open to the last page I’d studied, ready for me to pore over glyphs of life, death, and everything in between.
Vex’s purr softened into a murmur against my neck. “Is this what that strange golden message was about? Mister ‘The Universe’s One True Necromancer’...”
Her statement ended in her trademark beautiful giggles.
I grinned in return, laying a loving kiss against her temple. “Indeed, my sexy hex witch. Let’s see what this is truly about.”
Having said my piece, I willed the Codex to turn back to its beginning.

Its pages fluttered in reverse, turning one after another with quiet rustles that bled into whispers, like voices speaking in hushed tones just outside the realm of understanding. Then it stopped on the very first page. A single phrase was visible, written with letters made of glimmering blue text that might’ve been soul-light itself.
The soul is not a servant of rot.
True Necromancy is not the puppeteering of husks, nor the desecration of hollow bones.
It is the binding of essence to will, the shaping of that which lingers beyond the grave.
Flesh withers. Bone breaks. But the soul endures.
Seek not the rot that falls apart in your hands, but the light that refuses to fade.
Command not silence, but memory.
Do not raise the forgotten.
Reach for what remembers. Bind what still listens.

I stared at the text in silence. The message felt heavy, overly so. Not just because of its cryptic grandeur, but because some part of it rang true deep inside me. I wasn’t playing with puppets. True necromancy was learning how to command echoes of will, memory, and power.

Vex hummed beside me, still gently teasing my jewel sack with those soft, circling strokes of hers. “I can’t read a single word from this creepy book,” she revealed, sounding more curious than bothered.
“This text was probably meant to be read by me alone,” I replied before adding dryly, “Or maybe this is the work of just another one of my ‘primordial bullshit’ perks, as my girls like to call them.”
She grinned against my chest, purring louder, but at the same time, her grip on my balls tightened a bit, letting me know she wasn’t overly satisfied with my answer.

Whether she liked it or not, she had to admit that it made sense, though. My mind could process any language I encountered, so long as it wasn’t related to the supernatural, such as classes that produced runes or syllables. Kaelira’s Runeweaver Titan spells produced runes I couldn’t read, and so did Vex’s Hexwitch class, just with hexes replacing the runes.

It was most likely that the Codex spoke directly to my soul, but perhaps it was just written using some ancient text my primordial brain could translate for me. Either way, what mattered in the end was that the knowledge flowed.
The next few pages were straightforward. Four spells etched in clean, deliberate glyphs:
— [March of the Damned]
— [Awaken]
— [Soul Fusion]
— [Necromantic Codex]

They each carried their own diagrams and brief instructions, more meant to remind than to teach. It was clear I was meant to experiment on my own and come to my conclusions, not learn facts from a book.
I flipped to the next section.
A new heading appeared, engraved with solemn gravity:
> Necromantic Tier Ascension
To ascend to Tier II:
Possess 10 Elite Souls of Rank 3 or higher.

“These ranks again...” I murmured, remembering how my elite souls had ranks instead of levels. I had to collect 10 elite souls and upgrade them 2 ranks — if they didn’t come already ranked high enough to pass the requirement.
Then came the soul archives.

The first was the Lesser Soul Index. A glowing sea of names unfolded beneath it, over a million. All of them scorched to death by the firestorm I’d summoned in the heart of Lionheart. So many lives, snuffed out and absorbed. My Soul Reaper saber had claimed them all, and now I could use them as I wished through my magic.

I remembered using a hundred of these lesser souls to lock Sunfang in place, even if only briefly. They were loyal soldiers who didn’t fear death one bit, rushing into death’s embrace as if it meant nothing.
Then I turned the page to the second list.
A smaller title flared:
> Elite Soul Archive – Ascended Souls
— Foxkin Archer (Rank 1)
— Human Warrior (Rank 1)
I knew what would welcome my eyes here, yet I couldn’t help but blink.
I’d killed so many. Multiple were above level 40, higher leveled than me. And yet, only two entries. My brow furrowed.
Why?
What made a soul elite and not lesser? Why were only those two elites?

chapters.title: Chapter 780: Thinking Together
paragraphs: I narrowed my eyes at the meager list.
Just two elite souls. One of them, I was sure, had to be Veyrin. The foxkin prince I’d killed in our duel. But the human warrior? I had no idea. That mystery needed unraveling.
There was only one real way to figure it out.
With Vex still curled against me, I extended my free hand toward the open Codex.
“[Awaken].”

Mana surged up my spine into my hands, which then moved into the open Codex, feeding its pages with fuel. The symbols etched across the leather binding flared to life: pale veins of blue light traveled along its surface, reminding me of how lightning etched in flesh looked. The book hovered a little higher, vibrating faintly as it drank in the energy I provided.
Then, with a low, whispering hum, it responded to my call.

From its pages, a thin strand of spectral light uncoiled and slithered through the air, carving an arc to the spot I’d mentally chosen; the floor beyond the side of the mattress, just beyond Vex and me. The light spread toward the spot I willed it to, creating a small circle the size of a basketball ring.
And then she rose.
Not as some grotesque, monstrous entity that would fit in perfectly with the undead army of a Corpse Animator, but as something precise, cut from memory.
A female warrior stood before me.
She wore ghostly plated armor and a longsword hung at her side, spectral and weightless just like the rest of her.
Despite wearing armor from head to toe, her visor was raised, allowing me to see her face.
And I recognized her instantly.
She might’ve been pale blue, lacking the warmth of a living creature, but the sharp lines of her cheekbones, the defiant set of her jaw, and the braid of hair that once was golden blonde...
“Eve,” I said aloud, more in realization than greeting.

The bodyguard of the Greenvale twins. I’d killed her cleanly when I ambushed their ride traveling back home from the Grand Auction in the royal capital. I remembered how she’d stepped between me and her charges without hesitation. Noble-spirited. Loyal. Unquestioning. And now, she was here.
“Take off your helmet,” I ordered.
The soul obeyed without hesitation, with one hand lifting the phantom helm and letting it fall away into the ether. It seemed they could summon and de-summon their equipment.
Her face became clearer—well, as clear as a ghost could be. No doubt remained.
It was her.
“Do you understand me?”
No response.
Not a nod. Not a blink. Not even a flicker of her ethereal form.
I frowned.
The soul stood perfectly still, eyes locked forward, blade at rest. No will. No personality. Only form.
A puppet of memory, nothing more.
I stared at her, not understanding one thing.
Why was she here?
How had she become an Elite Soul?

She was barely in the level 30s when I’d slain her, if I remembered right. And it wasn’t some titanic battle either; there’d been no clash of wills or drawn-out struggle. I’d struck cleanly, decisively, and she’d died within seconds of our battle starting. That was it.

But during the war, I’d harvested the souls of warriors far more powerful. Late 30s. Even some in the mid 40s. Hundreds. And none of them had made it to this archive. None of them were included among the elite souls of my Necromantic Codex.
It made no sense.
My brow furrowed as I stared into her vacant eyes.

“Something wrong, hubby?” Vex murmured in a voice that was still husky from our recent indulgence, yet laced with a great deal of curiosity. Her hand left its previous post on my sack and rested against my chest, fingers tracing circles around my nipple.

“You look like you’re trying to solve a very hard puzzle.” She then giggled after landing a loving kiss on my cheek, “You look like a doggy trying to chew through the bone of a wyvern. It’s so adorable!”
... I didn’t know what to do with the weird image her final sentence created in my mind, so I elected to just ignore it and reply to her previous statement.

“I am. She shouldn’t be here. Not as an Elite. She wasn’t strong enough. I’ve killed dozens, no, hundreds, of enemies more powerful than her. Some were in the level 40s, yet they’re all considered lesser souls, like the ones I summoned to hold the Sunfang down. So why is she, a level 30 bodyguard I killed with little effort, considered an elite soul?”

Vex shifted her posture without offering a response to my question, rolling her body atop mine in one smooth motion. Her skin was warm against mine, and tantalizingly soft and supple where her delicious breasts were pressed against my chest. The heat of her bare lady flower brushed teasingly against my member, but this wasn’t her attempt at seduction.

She laid her hands flat against my chest, then lowered herself until her cheek rested just above my heart. Her eyes found mine. That mesmerizing, red gaze of hers was bright, sharp, and glittering with curiosity.

There was excitement there, yes, but not only the carnal kind. This was the thrill of discovery, of solving a riddle alongside someone she cherished greatly. A flicker of that signature mischief danced in her gaze as her smile curved upwards and she tilted her chin to nudge closer, her voice now a low, enthusiastic purr. “Let’s find it together. Just you and me, hubby~”
After she comfortably settled herself on top of me, she asked, “Are you sure strength is the only measure we should consider?”

I understood where she was going with her question, but I shook my head. “She wasn’t even close to the strongest opponent I’ve faced, and she was just a simple bodyguard. The twins have told me she was on their payroll, but their father had much stronger bodyguards. They didn’t take those guards with them out of pure hubris.”
“The twins?” Vex raised an eyebrow.
“Oh.” It was only now that I realized I still owed my sexy woman a few stories. “Long story short, I kidnapped and enslaved the Greenvale twins. They’re under my control now.”
“...” A completely flabbergasted face welcomed my declaration.

Amara Valessia Arvanelle Greenvale
Vivienne Valessia Arvanelle Greenvale

“There’s a time and place for jokes.”

“V-V-V-Vex the H-H-Hexblade?!!!!!!!”
She practically shrieked the name.

Of course she knew Vex. Anyone who’d ever walked past a guard station had seen that face on a wanted poster. Her crimes were legendary, her bounty outrageous. She wasn’t just a criminal but a national scandal.
Vex didn’t react. Didn’t even spare the duke’s daughter a glance.
Instead, she let out a sigh and pinched my cheeks like a mother scolding her mischievous child.

I laughed. “You caught me...”
She arched a brow and flicked her eyes toward the gate. “Why didn’t you bring the other sister?”

“... I know that. So?” she asked, genuinely confused.
“I can’t have my women ogled by lecherous eyes.”

But Amara wasn’t listening.

I sighed.
A flick of my fingers conjured a strong burst of chilled water that splashed across her face like a bucket of ice.
She squeaked like a startled cat and stumbled back into the portal with a yelp.
The gate vanished behind her.
How she would explain her drenched dress after excusing herself to the restroom didn’t cross my mind. I’m sure she would find a good excuse.
Silence returned.

Vex’s eyes turned inquisitive again, her joyful gaze slowly transforming into something more thoughtful.
“Hubby...” she whispered slowly, her fingers still tracing idle patterns on my cheeks, “why do I see the names of your lovers among your [Subjugated] people?”

chapters.title: Chapter 782: Sexy Slave Girls [Bonus]
paragraphs: I shrugged my shoulders dismissively. “What do you think? They’re my sexy slave girls, of course.”

“...” A deadpan stare welcomed my explanation before she sighed defeatedly, “I truly fell for a horrible thug of a man, didn’t I? The influence those trio of crazy chicks had on me can no longer be denied... I have the worst taste in men.”

I smiled once again, though not with amusement this time. It was a quiet, crooked smile, full of things left unsaid. My hands roamed along the curves of her butt, until finding the entrance to her backdoor, which they began eagerly massaging.

At the same time, Vex’s expression shifted, going from a face full of mischief to one that spoke of horror. Just as my index finger found itself lined up perfectly with her entrance and began its descent, an alarmed yelp sounded in my ears. “Kya!!! Okay, I got it! You’re an awesome boyfriend, not a horrible thug of a man!”
“And what about your taste in men?” I asked with narrowed eyes.
“I only settle for the very best! Whoever is the greatest man in the universe shall receive my maidenhood!”
Hearing her words, my finger stopped its descent and retreated. At the same time, I nodded, with a satisfied smile returning to my lips. “Good girl.”
She giggled lightly, enjoying our playful banter. Afterward, she tilted her head to the side. “So... is there a benefit to being one of your ‘sexy slave girls,’ then?”
“A few. I grant all my subjugated companions telepathy with me and with each other. They can speak to me at any time, from anywhere. Well, unless I leave this world.”
Her eyebrows rose.

“That’s not all,” I continued, brushing her white hair back behind her ear. “I can see and feel through their senses using [Overlord’s Eyes]. And, if I wish, I can lend a portion of my power to them through [Overlord’s Magnanimity]. Boost their stats with mine. Strengthen them.”
“That’s extremely powerful!” she shouted, clearly surprised by it.
“It’s a primordial class for a reason... [Overlord’s Sacrifice] lets me take on any damage directed at them.”
Instead of remaining surprised, she pouted, poking me in the nose. “It’s basically like the hex curse I gifted you to celebrate our union. Not fair.”
“Yours has more utility,” I assured her. “It works on mana depletion and hunger, too. Mine doesn’t.”

That earned me a satisfied, genuine grin. Her red eyes gleamed like twin rubies in the low light of the basement now that the ritual circle was no longer brightening the room. She leaned in even further against me in a needy manner.
Then, in a much quieter voice, she whispered, “Could I... also be one of them?”
I paused.
No teasing. No flirtation. Just a request, offered gently.
I didn’t answer with words. I simply sent her a [Subjugation] request.
It let her choose her own terms. No chains. No bindings. She could write it on her own terms, if she wished to accept.
Her breath hitched. Slowly, her eyes began shining with more and more determination as she willed her mind to click on ‘Accept.’
Nothing happened.
We both blinked.
A small alert blinked red in my vision.
[ERROR: Insufficient Subjugation Capacity]
[The discrepancy between Subjugator and Target is too large. Capacity exceeded.]
I stared at the message with wry eyes.
Vex’s smile returned, as mischievous as ever this time. “Wait, let me guess, hubby~ This wifey of yours is way too strong for you, hmm?”

“Your silence is louder than a thousand words,” she giggled. But then, her fingers began tracing idle shapes across my skin as she rolled off my chest, landing nestled up against my side. “Moving back onto our original topic, about the reason why a weak bodyguard became an Elite Soul while strong lionkin soldiers ended up being Lesser ones...”
She stared up at the ceiling, thinking for a dozen or so seconds, after which she parted her delicate lips.
“Maybe it wasn’t about power.”
I turned my head toward her. “What do you mean?”

“Think about who she was,” Vex said, gesturing toward Eve’s soul. “She was the personal bodyguard to the Greenvale twins. That family’s not some merchant house from the countryside. They’re royal dukes. Eve didn’t just swing a sword; she held status. Trust. A place close to the heart of one of the kingdom’s pillars.”
The realization struck like thunder rumbling through a closed cathedral.
“She mattered,” I said slowly.
Vex nodded. “Exactly. You killed many stronger lionkin, but were any of them more important?”

“...No.” I thought back to the battlefield. “They were soldiers. Mid-tier. Some squad leaders, maybe. Not generals. Not nobles. The elites of the lionkin army could tank my firestorm and wait out its duration by moving outside its range. The only named ones who died in that blaze were the lower-ranked.”
“And what about that foxkin archer?” she asked.
“Prince Veyrin,” I replied. “He was their chief’s son.”

“There you go, hubby. My hunch tells me that this isn’t about levels but about weight. Not physical, but spiritual. Narrative. Fate. Whatever it is that spins the world, maybe it values certain deaths more than others. Killing a blade trusted by important people is valued differently from killing a hundred regular soldiers.”
I stared at Eve again. This time, I saw her not as a mistake in the Codex, but as a message.
A ghost, yes. But a meaningful one.
“I think you’re right,” I murmured.

“Of course I’m right, when am I not?” Vex purred smugly, curling closer against my side again. “What kind of necromancer would you be without your sexy hex witch by your side to explain the rules of your own magic?”
I chuckled, but even as I pulled her tighter, my mind drifted. The Codex hadn’t just shown me a soul.
It had given me a clue.
To bolster my necromantic army, I had to collect the souls of important people.
Then, my focus shifted. Not to Vex, but toward another spell in my Necromantic Codex.
[Soul Fusion].
It was time to see how soul upgrading worked!

chapters.title: Chapter 783: [Soul Fusion]
paragraphs: Type: Active – Soul Upgrade
Cost: Variable Mana (based on fusion size)
Requirement: Target [Elite Soul] + at least 3 compatible [Lesser Souls]

[Initiates a ritualistic merge of multiple [Lesser Souls] into a single [Elite Soul]. The process strengthens the target soul, enhancing its stats and abilities. Souls consumed in fusion are permanently destroyed.]

I re-opened the [Necromantic Codex] with nothing but a thought. As it wasn’t the focus of our conversation for the past few minutes, I’d sent it to rest on a nearby table, not wanting to converse with a floating tome in front of our faces.

Upon my command, its spectral pages unfurled in the air before me, etched with script that only I could read. Next, I focused my will, and three lesser souls floated into view on the ethereal parchment, each name highlighted by the codex’s ghostly blue light.
[Selected Souls:]
[Lionkin Beggar – Level 1 – Potency: 2]
[Lionkin Housewife – Level 1 – Potency: 3]
[Lionkin Butcher – Level 1 – Potency: 4]
They were the most meager members of my soul collection—save for the souls of lionkin children, almost all of whom had only 1 Potency to them—but even scraps had value. Or at least I hoped so.
Target: [Elite Soul – Eve] – Rank 1
With a mental nudge, I initiated the [Soul Fusion].

The selected lesser souls shimmered and materialized into the room from the pages of the ancient tome. This itself was quite the curious event in my eyes, because technically, it wasn’t the Codex that housed the souls but my saber, the Mythic-rarity Soul Reaper.

My working theory was that the Necromantic Codex acted as a proxy, allowing me to do my soul magic without having to summon the saber from my pocket ring. It’s as if the two worked together seamlessly to make my life easier, transferring souls between one another without trouble.

The three souls that materialized didn’t resemble the shapes of their physical forms. There were no faces, no hands, no eyes. Just three pale orbs of light, each one a bit different in its hue and intensity.

The beggar’s orb was dull and small, sporting a sickly grayish blue color; the housewife’s was slightly warmer, having a soft amber in it; the butcher’s was brighter, letting a few red-tinted lines don the otherwise blue orb.
They hovered for a moment, then began to tremble.

Without any further warning, they collided in a rather violent manner. The fusion looked more like a massacre than a peaceful merging, like one soul was devouring the others while they each writhed in agony. Threads of spectral matter tore and tangled between them.
Muffled screams echoed from within the orbs, echoes that weren’t truly sound, just psychic impressions of fear and confusion the souls experienced in their final moments.
The resulting orb had quite a sickly, dull color to it. It looked weak. Once the combination had completed, it began to slowly drift toward Eve.
She waited without a single motion of her body. The fused orb entered her chest. Her form suddenly glowed with pale light—only briefly, only weakly—but enough to show it had worked.
Nothing dramatic. No leap in power. Her blue body didn’t suddenly gain more contrast or definition.
*Shh!*
All of a sudden, something strange occurred.

Tiny specks that were the size of sand grains began to rise from Eve’s form. They had not the blue light reminiscent of souls, but an ethereal white, nearly invisible to the naked eye unless one focused on them.
There were thousands upon thousands of these particles leaving Eve’s body.

They drifted upward in silence, seeming to be entirely weightless. They passed through the ceiling as though the stone and wood above meant nothing to them. As though the world itself had no right to obstruct their path.
They were gone in seconds. No fanfare. No sound. No pain. Just... release.
Then the [Necromantic Codex] stirred.
Its pages fluttered violently without my command, flipping faster than any hand could manage. It opened to a fresh page. It was a blank spread, unmarred by ink or glyph.
And then, it began to write by itself, as if me experiencing this phenomenon was needing to unlock this knowledge.
The soul-blue color etched itself into the parchment in flowing glyphs and looping characters, appearing ancient and dignified.
True Necromancy is not the Devourer’s Path.
He who bindeth flesh to bone alone hath not earned the name of Death’s Keeper.
To rend the soul is easy. One need only erase the flesh that houseth it.
But to cleanse souls... that is an undertaking most arduous.
Let it be known: the [Soul Fusion] is no crime against the order of the universe. It hindereth not life.
For a necromancer is no pest, no leech, no plague to be hunted by kings and their armies.
It is the Corpse Animators who art an affront to life’s sanctity, treating the living as fuel for undead armies.
For every Lesser Soul consumed in true [Soul Fusion], their sin is unbound.
They are cast not to the pit, nor trapped in waiting, but lifted.
Expedited, cleansed, and returned unto the hands of the Shepherds of Rebirth, prepared to rejoin the cycle of life.
Thou art no enemy of life, if so thou choosest.
Death, in thy hands, need not be desecration. It may yet be release.
I stared at the page in silence for a few seconds before my brain began putting the puzzle pieces together.
“So that’s what those particles were...”
“What do you mean, Quin?” Vex asked, confused.
Instead of replying immediately, I stood from the mattress and moved toward Eve. I placed my palm above her head, and just as expected, the particles passed through my skin without any difficulty.

“These tiny grains were souls, yes, but not the fused parts, not the power fed into Eve. They are the remnants. By using [Soul Fusion], I’ve cleansed the souls, carving all the corrupted parts off of them. Their experiences, their levels, and their thoughts... they were all used up during the merging.”

I paused for a moment, examining Eve’s emotionless, ghostly face. “What remained behind was their souls in their purest form. It is the Goddess, Lilyanna, who is supposed to oversee this cleansing process. After this process, they’re ready to be reborn. What the text said was “They are cast not to the pit, nor trapped in waiting, but lifted. Expedited, cleansed, and returned unto the hands of the Shepherds of Rebirth, prepared to rejoin the cycle of life.” By completing the cleansing process in the Goddess’ stead, I expedited the process of rebirth. The Goddess oversees billions of souls; there must be a queue waiting for her to cleanse them, especially if something else demands her attention.”
A smirk found its way onto my features as I announced, “I made them skip the queue.”

“Based on your overly cocky grin, I’m gonna assume you’d once again done something amazing,” Vex said while following my path from the mattress, standing next to me with her hand in mine. She directed her gaze toward Eve, but when observing the Awakened Soul didn’t observe her to glean any further information, her attention found its way to me. “I’m gonna need a time-out, hubby. Goddess Liliyanna? Soul Ecosystem? Rebirth?”

chapters.title: Chapter 784: Upgrading My Elites
paragraphs: Her voice sounded utterly lost, letting me know that not even Black Fang’s dusty tomes held this knowledge. Or, at the very least, the purple-eyed, horribly antisocial, and, Goddess help me, turbo hot milf didn’t share it with Vex.
Anyhow. I’d already decided to trust this awesome existence, so I spent the next few minutes delivering my information about all that I’d kept from her regarding this topic.

Once I was done delivering the truths of the universe, such as the almighty Goddess they all revered as if she were some all-knowing, omnipresent entity, was a brat in need of severe correction in reality, Vex stood silent for a moment with her eyes wide and face pale. Her lips parted, and the first thing out of her mouth was:
“I need a drink.”

Without waiting for my response, she spun on her heel and strutted across the room with her hips swaying in rhythmic motions that would capture the attention of any man. She moved toward a wide, reinforced barrel nestled into the corner, one I had assumed held wine or something equivalent.
A pop of suction echoed as she twisted the tap embedded into the wood, filling a crystal glass with a dark crimson liquid.

She raised the glass to her lips, took a sip, and her entire body immediately relaxed. Color returned to her face like a tide rushing in. Her cheeks flushed a warm pink, and a breathy murmur escaped her lips.
“Ah... So tasty.”
But as she turned back toward me, still sipping, my nose twitched. There was something off about the scent. Metallic. Tangy.
“Why,” I asked slowly, “do I smell blood?”
She gave a light shrug of her bare shoulder, utterly unbothered.
“Oh, I mix in a bit of lionkin blood. Just a dash. Makes it more satisfying to drink.”
“... That sounds like it would be horrible.”

“It might have an unconventional taste, but I find it more delicious than the Molten Anvil Mead I shared with you guys in the bath.” She smiled and raised the glass toward me in invitation. “Wanna try? It’s fresh. Don’t worry, no plague, no rot. I added a preservation crystal to it. Breaks down pathogens, keeps the blood from coagulating, and locks in the flavor profile.”
I declined the offer with a shake of my head, watching her take another contented sip after murmuring, “More for me, I suppose.”

Honestly, I wasn’t overly shocked to learn she drinks the blood of slain lionkin. After all, crossing the border and going on a murder spree until she passes out from exhaustion is her ideal holiday vacation. Or at least that was the case before today. With their Sunfang executed, their capital city burned to the ground, and their people actively being hunted by their fellow beastkin, her need for vengeance has been satisfied.
With her wine glass in hand, she moved back toward me.
Now that the fusion was complete, I turned my attention back to the [Necromantic Codex] and navigated to the page of Elite Souls, where I focused on Eve’s name in particular.
[Elite Soul – Eve]
[Type: Warrior]
[Soul Rank: 1]
[Fusion Progress: 0.001 / 1000]
Her page opened with a soft shimmer, displaying the bare-bones statistics of her existence. A single thin bar glowed beneath the header. It was so faint, I had to focus to see it at all.
The progress indicator had nudged forward by the slimmest margin. From nothing to something. 0.001 out of 1000. A single drop in an ocean.
The [Soul Fusion] had worked, but it also made one thing painfully clear.
The ranking-up of Elite Souls was mercilessly slow without the right fuel. Civilian souls barely registered as kindling.
Still... kindling could build a fire.
And I had a million more to burn.
But before I started blasting, I wanted to experiment a bit more.
With her wine glass in hand and that satisfied blush still warming her cheeks, Vex leaned against the wall beside me and observed as I selected the next candidates.
“Let’s see what better fuel looks like,” I muttered, summoning three souls. Warriors, all of them. Level 10, each with a Potency Rating of 20.
I selected Eve’s name once more and cast [Soul Fusion].
The process of soul merging happened once again, with the resulting single orb entering Eve’s body. The progress bar ticked upward, ever so slightly more noticeable than before.
[Fusion Progress: 0.001 → 0.161 / 1000]

So that’s what better material looks like. It wasn’t a flood, not even close. But it was the difference between a single raindrop... and a modest splash. At the end of the day, level 10 Warriors weren’t exactly rare. I believed that it was fair to assume that this soul necromancy business was meant to be more than me going around hunting level 10 rookies.

Wishing to study one particular theory of mine, I conjured three more souls. They were of the same level, same potency, but this time, they were non-warriors. An Archer, a Mage, and a Tank. Their forms shimmered less potently, more passive in their energy.
I performed the fusion again.
A quieter resonance welcomed the fusion, and the increase was noticeably weaker.
[Fusion Progress: 0.161 → 0.2 / 1000]
Just 0.04. As opposed to the previous 0.16 increase. This meant only one thing: with the same level and potency, the soul’s class greatly affected the result.

So... role alignment mattered. Warrior souls fed Warrior Elites better. There was likely a deeper compatibility layer beneath that, too. Maybe specific traits, emotional resonance, perhaps even shared kills.
With a quiet flick of my wrist, my robe materialized from the void of my pocket ring.

Without a word, I stepped behind Vex and draped it gently over her shoulders, covering her naked form. I ensured it was closed in front of her body, hiding her most sensitive areas. She blinked, puzzled.
“I wasn’t cold...”
I didn’t answer.
Instead, I extended my hand forward and channeled power into the air. “[Awaken].”

A surge of soul energy swirled at my command, coalescing in front of us until the blue form of the second Elite Soul emerged. It was a tall, noble figure with fox ears, a princely mane of silver-streaked auburn hair, and a well-kept, lush tail trailing behind him.
Vex looked at the newly arrived soul warrior. Then looked at herself, still holding the edges of my oversized robe around her body.
Realization dawned across her face.
“Wait. Wait a second.” She turned toward me slowly, brows lifting. “Did you seriously make me cover up... because you didn’t want your own soul soldier seeing your woman naked?”
I offered no defense for my case. No apology, either.
Instead, I grinned, shamelessly ignoring any further inquiry she might’ve had for me regarding the topic. “My tome is way too hefty. I say it’s time we reduce its page count!”
With a mental command, the [Necromantic Codex] flipped open again. I navigated to Veyrin’s page.
[Elite Soul – Veyrin]
Type: Archer
Soul Rank: 1
Fusion Progress: 0.000 / 1000
I raised my hand.

A flood of light surged from my soul storage as I selected and summoned one hundred thousand Level 1 Lesser Souls. Their potency was minimal as weak civilians, but together, they formed a glowing, buzzing storm of potential.
With a sweeping gesture, I funneled the entire mass toward Veyrin.
“Let’s see if a hundred thousand nobodies can build a prince,” I murmured.
And cast [Soul Fusion].

chapters.title: Chapter 785: Fusion Mechanics [Bonus]
paragraphs: [Elite Soul – Veyrin]
Type: Archer
Soul Rank: 1
Fusion Progress: 0.000 / 1000
I raised my hand.

A flood of light surged outward as I selected and summoned a hundred thousand Level 1 civilian souls. They were dim, flickering things—barely more than whispers, really—but together, they became a thunderous storm rumbling in the air.
“Let’s see if a hundred thousand nobodies can build a prince,” I murmured.

The entire storm collapsed inward in a dazzling burst of pale-blue light. The resonance was subtle but steady: no grand shockwaves, no bursts of power, but a silent, consistent force as the souls funneled into their new host.
The Codex responded.
[Fusion Progress: 0.000 → 33.333 / 1000]

I raised an eyebrow. I knew that the math was more or less in line with the previous experiment, but the fact that the souls of a large city’s worth of citizens gave only a 3% progress toward the next rank was hard to wrap my mind around.
And yet, curiosity still prodded at me.
What if a different Elite Soul had a better affinity for the fodder? Did the soul’s archetype matter at all when the source was too weak to contain a combat class?
To test it, I summoned another hundred thousand Level 1 souls—identical in level and potency—and repeated the process, targeting Eve this time. The fusion took them in just as cleanly.
[Fusion Progress: 0.2 → 33.541 / 1000]
Only a minor increase in the amount gained compared to Veyrin.

So, based on my data gleaned from my two test subjects, my findings indicated that no, there was no hidden multiplier. Any marginal benefit from affinity only activated when the source had something more to offer. For cannon fodder, it didn’t matter who the target was. Though, of course, to solidify this theory, more tests would have to be conducted once I acquired different Elite Souls.
To clear the soul clutter, I began compressing my reserves. With the same motion, I summoned all remaining Level 1 civilian souls, save for three.
The basement under Vex’s mansion lit up like I’d just set off a massive amount of fireworks all at once as over one million spirits coalesced in the air.
I placed them all into Veyrin.

Trillions upon trillions of tiny white particles began to drift from Veyrin’s body, rising in silence like dust caught in sunbeams. They shone with a faint light as they rose upward, spiraling toward the heavens in a slow, unending ascent.
The cleansing.
I watched them with folded arms and a small smile tugging at my lips.
Maybe Lilyanna wouldn’t have to throw a hissy fit after all. I wasn’t stealing her souls; I was doing her job for her. Picking up the slack. Processing the backlog. Expediting judgment.

Hell, I was practically a glorified garbage man. A custodian cleaning the filth from the world, soul by soul. The lionkin scum had spent their lives distributing pain and bloodshed to all unfortunate enough to come across their paths. Truth be told, they were nothing but a waste of oxygen that dragged the world down with them, as far as I was concerned. Now, even their deaths served a purpose.
“I recycle,” I murmured, watching the purified fragments fade into the sky. “Green necromancy. Environmentally friendly with a strong focus on sustainability ”

I grinned wider, still staring at the fading light. Somewhere far above, the ‘Shepherd of Rebirth’ would be receiving a large shipment of souls that was already pre-cleansed, pre-packaged, and ready to go.

“You’re welcome, Lilyanna,” I said, placing a hand over my heart and offering an exaggerated salute to the sky. “Keep the line moving, my fellow recycler. Let’s be good colleagues, you and I. And while you’re at it, think over your decision to deny me the Healer class, will you?”

“It’s time for a refill...” Vex muttered dryly as she began walking back toward her stock of lionkin blood wine—or whatever it was called. As soon as she heard my sacrilegious words aimed at the divine entity she thought to be something akin to what the Soul Records is in reality, her brain needed a break. It would take her some getting used to before she could accept it, by the look of things.

Now, why did I give Veyrin the entire stock of my weak souls? Because most of the lionkin were brutes with a warrior-esque fighting style. Meaning they should provide Eve with higher fusion efficiency. There weren’t many rangers among their ranks, thus it was better to bolster Veyrin with the mass of civilian souls.

The [Necromantic Codex] activated itself as page after page began to dissolve, the blue ink of names evaporating into nothing. It was a silent exodus of a million souls who had been quietly erased and processed.
A minute ago, my Codex had been bloated, unwieldy.
Now it was sleek. Lighter. Emptier.

Only about two hundred thousand names remained, and all of them stood apart from the rabble I had just dumped into Veyrin’s soul. These souls had lived just long enough, fought just hard enough, and killed just viciously enough to matter, becoming level 2 or higher.
They were stronger. Denser. Worth more.
And that meant one thing: Eve was about to have a feast.

The [Necromantic Codex] floated before me, suspended in the air. Despite my mass recycling, its pages were still engraved with a nearly endless list of names. Even with most of the weak ones fed to Veyrin, the codex still contained more pages than I’d preferred.
‘Too bloated. Give me a proper summary of the remaining souls in inventory.’

With a mental push of intent, I willed the tome to shift. The current page faded into light, and the paper curled backward on its own, like wind-blown parchment. Dozens more turned in rapid succession until they stopped on a fresh page. At the top, neat text appeared as if being typed out by an invisible hand.
[Soul Inventory Summary – Lesser Souls]

Below it, rows of elegant script began forming into a categorized table. The codex was obeying, sorting my horde of souls not by name, but by level range, just like I’d envisioned. It did the work for me, skipping past the mess of names and diving straight into usefulness.
(Picture)

I nodded with satisfaction as my eyes scanned the clean breakdown. This was what I needed: order. Not just a book that displayed a mountain of random souls, but a toolkit. Something I could wield with surgical precision.

The sheer number of level 2–9 souls dwarfed the rest, just as expected. Most successful civilians and weak warriors should reach a few levels even with their civilian classes, such as Aurora, who was level 5 when we met, despite being an Alchemist who never once collected XP by killing. Merchants, thieves, and even prostitutes could obtain classes that were designed to help them with their profession. As such, any person talented in their craft (that was recognized as a profession by the Soul Records) had the chance to level up at least a few times.
I willed the Codex to invest the souls I needed—low-level Warriors whose Potency stat averaged fifteen. I chose to use ten thousand of them.
The selected souls spiraled upward like a vortex, drawn into a swirling storm above her waiting vessel after I cast [Soul Fusion].

I glanced back at the Codex, mentally calling for another round. This time, I made some calculations and chose 14,250 more Warrior souls of 15 average potency, selecting from a pool of 10 to 25 potency warriors. The 10 potency holders were level 2 warriors, while the 25 potency holders were level 12.
The Codex obeyed, flicking to the right entry and highlighting the appropriate pool of names.
Another surge of souls merged together to form a blue orb that moved toward Eve before vanishing into her body.
[Fusion Progress: 430.218 → 1000 / 1000]
The moment her bar hit max, the transformation began.

Eve’s thus farm expressionless, motionless form shuddered violently. Her frame was engulfed in bright spectral light, then sharpened like a lens sliding into focus. Her features grew more defined. Where once she had been a ghostly blur with bare silhouette, now her face held significantly more recognizable details: a stern brow, full lips, strong jawline. Her posture straightened, and properties of the armor she wore in her final moments began to coalesce across her limbs, regaining a portion of their physical color and hardness.

Unlike her equipment, however, her skin remained the same muted soul-blue. She still didn’t speak, didn’t show emotions, and held no trace of her former self’s memories or personality. But she no longer looked like an eerie ghost. She looked like a proper soul warrior.
[Elite Soul – Eve]
Soul Rank: 2
Type: Warrior
Fusion Progress: 0 / 2000
I extended a hand toward her. “Punch my palm.”

A flood of light surged outward as I selected and summoned a hundred thousand Level 1 civilian souls.
They were dim, flickering things—barely more than whispers, really—but together, they became a thunderous storm rumbling in the air.
“Let’s see if a hundred thousand nobodies can build a prince,” I murmured.
The entire storm collapsed inward in a dazzling burst of pale-blue light.
The resonance was subtle but steady: no grand shockwaves, no bursts of power, but a silent, consistent force as the souls funneled into their new host.
The Codex responded.
[Fusion Progress: 0.000 → 33.333 / 1000]
I raised an eyebrow.

I knew that the math was more or less in line with the previous experiment, but the fact that the souls of a large city’s worth of citizens gave only a 3% progress toward the next rank was hard to wrap my mind around.
And yet, curiosity still prodded at me.
What if a different Elite Soul had a better affinity for the fodder?
Did the soul’s archetype matter at all when the source was too weak to contain a combat class?
To test it, I summoned another hundred thousand Level 1 souls—identical in level and potency—and repeated the process, targeting Eve this time.
The fusion took them in just as cleanly.
[Fusion Progress: 0.2 → 33.541 / 1000]
Only a minor increase in the amount gained compared to Veyrin.
So, based on my data gleaned from my two test subjects, my findings indicated that no, there was no hidden multiplier.
Any marginal benefit from affinity only activated when the source had something more to offer.

chapters.title: Chapter 786: Might of Elite Souls [Bonus]
paragraphs: She obeyed immediately, with no hesitation whatsoever. Her ghostly fist collided with my outstretched palm, and I felt it: solid weight, dense power, and a proper form was behind the strike. She didn’t just look stronger. She was stronger.
I flexed my fingers, letting the stinging sensation settle. “I estimate her to be about level 30, stats-wise at least.”
The Codex moved back into my vision at my mental command. I willed it to display the data from the two batches I’d just used. It obeyed with a shimmer of blue light, presenting a refined breakdown.
📜 [Codex Entry: Invested Warrior Souls – Eve]
Levels 2–4: 12,000 souls invested.
Levels 5–9: 8,000 souls invested.
Levels 10–14: 4,250 souls invested.
Total invested soul count: 24,250
Satisfied, I nodded to myself. All from the collection of lower-tier souls, as planned. It was a good baseline test.
Next, I selected another batch: 10,000 more warriors from the same tier. Low-level. Potency 15 average. I wanted to see if the returns were the same.
I cast [Soul Fusion] again.
The souls rose upward, swirling into another orb of light that merged cleanly into Eve’s waiting body.
A moment later, the Codex delivered the new result:
[Fusion Progress: 0 → 200 / 2000]
My eyes narrowed.
Same potency. Same type. But... only half the progress.
Sensing a bad omen, I ventured to unearth what was going on. I had kept three low-potency civilian souls, saved for this moment exactly.
I offered them to Eve.
[ERROR: Level 1 Lesser souls cannot be used on Rank 2 or higher Elite Souls.]
... So that was it.
My heart felt heavy as the full meaning settled in.
This was no simple grind. The system wouldn’t let me throw garbage into the forge and expect steel on the other end. Just like my own leveling journey, my soul army’s growth was tied to quality.

As the Codex had earlier decreed, a true necromancer wasn’t a parasite feeding off the scraps of society. I wasn’t supposed to pillage weak cities and cull civilians like some opportunistic warlock desperate for power. That wasn’t how true necromancers worked.
I was meant to hunt worthy targets.
That was why, instead of 400 progress, Eve only gained 200.
That was why civilian souls didn’t work at all.
“I get it now...”
Knowing the first three tiers of souls in my inventory faced lesser gains on a rank 2 Elite Soul, I elected to use the next three tiers instead.
First came 4,000 warriors between levels 15 and 19, averaging 30 Potency each.
Then, 2,000 warriors between levels 20 and 24, with an average Potency of 45.
And finally, 1,000 warriors between levels 25 and 29, each boasting around 70 Potency.
Once selected, the Codex lit up with spectral light, the names of the chosen offerings flickering and then fading as the souls were claimed.
[Fusion Progress: 200 → 946.20 / 2000]

Damn. Only 746 progress for offering so many souls that were of her type to boot! Soul upgrades were one costly investment, that was for sure. I invested all my warrior-type souls into Eve in this level range, earning her another 750 progress.
I then filled the remaining bar of 300 progress with 1100 level 30-34, 100 potency souls.
[Fusion Progress: 2000 / 2000]
The moment Eve’s progress bar hit full again, the transformation kicked in. This time, it was even more vivid than before.

Where before only fragments of her armor had materialized, those pieces now thickened, connected, and expanded with a wave of spectral reinforcement. A sheen of brilliant steel spread from her shoulders down her arms, encasing her in what now looked like fully-restored war gear. Her gauntlets gleamed from their polishing. The etchings across her breastplate pulsed with soul light. The long sword at her hip, which was half-transparent after her first rank-up, solidified into a pristine weapon.
But even with her arms and armor now fully restored, her skin remained that distinctive soul-blue. Still ethereal. Still otherworldly.

Her face, though... her face was no longer washed out. It was fully defined. A sharp jawline, high cheekbones, eyes that held a firm spectral glow. She looked like a soul brought back in her prime. Strong, imposing, undeniably elite.
Vex took a slow step forward, observing Eve from different angles with an arched brow, then turned her red eyes to me.
“Quin. Have her punch me instead of you,” she asked abruptly.
“...You sure?”
“Yes. Punch me. Not you. Let’s see what she can do.”
I frowned. “Is this about protecting me?”
Vex paused for a second before a troubled expression emerged on her delicate face. “You’re a sharp one... I hoped you wouldn’t realize.”

She then smirked, “Please, swallow your manly ego for me, love. I’m almost two hundred years older than you. There’s no shame in being a bit weaker than me. It should be me who feels insecure, after all, in few more years and you’ll make my past two centuries spent in the pursuit of personal strength look like a joke, the work of an amateur.”
She stepped up beside me and added, with a wink, “Plus, it makes me feel warm inside to know that I protect my man.”

I had to grimace inwardly. I already felt weird about her ‘gift’ to me, the curse where she made it so she would suffer alongside me should I be in danger. But I knew Vex. She wasn’t a fragile princess but a warrior woman. Just like I had an innate desire to protect my girls, she felt the same way about me. So I didn’t have it in me to question or deny her gift, nor oppose her most recent statement.
Instead, I sighed defeatedly under my breath before nodding toward Eve. “Punch her palm.”
Eve obeyed immediately.
Her armored fist shot forward and slammed into Vex’s outstretched hand.
*Thwack!*
The impact sounded like a hammer striking metal. The air rippled. Dust kicked up at their feet.
Vex’s arm trembled slightly from the impact. Her eyes narrowed in deliberation.
She flexed her fingers slowly and muttered, “That one hurt... Not enough to leave a mark, but still...”
After she was done shaking her wrists, she looked back at me. “She’s strong. Very strong. I’d put her Strength stat somewhere around a level 45 to 50 warrior.”
A satisfied grin crept onto my lips.
“Then I didn’t waste those thousands of souls after all.”
*Brrrt!* Vex’s communication artifact rang all of a sudden. “Damn it!” She cursed under her breath.
“What’s up?” I asked, surprised at her reaction.
“I had this damn thing on what I like to call ‘Fuck off’ mode, or ‘Do Not Disturb’ as the posh folks say. If it rang anyway, that means it’s a real emergency.
“Oh.”
“Indeed...” she sighed before picking up. “Big sis, I’m on my honeymoon, you know? We just came back from the mission, too! What’s so important for you to disturb me?”

Orianna’s voice responded. She wasn’t impressed. “Your mission ended days ago. Staying in lionkin lands and playing soldier was your choice, on your own time. As for honeymoon... Congrats, Vex. From the bottom of my heart, I’m happy for you. But I can’t let you enjoy it now.”
She finished her statement with a defeated sigh, sounding sincere about her words.

“You’ll have to postpone it because the Greenvales have declared official war on us, and thanks to that loser Maelstrom suffering over 15,000 casualties during the beastkin outing, we went from feeling confident about this prospective conflict to being the clear underdogs. He lost over 50 Veil Walkers, for the Goddess’ sake! If that wasn’t bad enough, our newly acquired beastkin allies had suffered great casualties in the war, save for the wolfkin and dogkin. They won’t be able to rush to our rescue immediately. I need you to help me reorganize our defenses around the most valuable outposts.”
Vex’s face went pale.
But she wasn’t alone.
Mine had as well.

After all, this was solely my doing. And now I brought the Vesper Consortium into a war neither side wanted to fight. The mediator, the man seated in the highest position among the seven circle heads, wanted to avoid war. Alastair Greenvale and his advisors wanted to avoid the war.

It was I who wanted them to clash, because I needed a large-scale conflict so that I could flourish. To that end, I paused my sentence of the twins and let them stay the night at home to rile the duke up by begging to sleep in his room and pretending to have nightmares from the kidnapping attempt that I made them think the finance department head masterminded, when it was me who did it.

But I’d already gotten my large-scale clash in the lands of the Beastman Confederation. Now, I planned to lean back for a bit and focus on my upcoming Primordial Rank-Up mission while letting my girls get more familiar with their classes.
So... I just made the duke declare war on a weakened Consortium, while my Ascendants and I might not even participate in the whole thing if the primordial trial takes too long to complete.
Well, what can I say?
... Oopsie?

I hope the soul fusion stuff wasn’t too nerdy! Let me know if they were. Don’t worry, I can take the criticism. The primordial trials are about to begin, and I have incredibly big plans for it this time around!!
On another note, the many super gifts you amazing guys gave the novel has given it the best days ever recorded, the numbers are literally peaking right now.
Thanks for all the support!

chapters.title: Chapter 787: Call of Duty
paragraphs: “... Got it,” Vex sighed, looking at me apologetically. She clearly wished to stay with me longer, but duty called. Not only was she a high-ranking member, but also the third most important member of the drug department. At times, she simply had to be present.
“I understand. Don’t worry about it. We can resume our honeymoon at any time,” I said, stroking her hair in my palm before landing a loving kiss on the top of her head.

A gentle smile was the response my actions received before she excused herself and went to the back room, preparing herself to head out. Despite her eccentric persona, she very clearly cared about her image as a youthful and sexy woman. As such, she had to fix her ruined makeup and cleanse her body of our bodily fluids, among other things...
“Haaah... Women, am I right?”
Neither of my soul elites responded. How boring.
While waiting for Vex, I decided to use my time smartly, because if there was one thing I knew about women was that they needed a lot more time to get prepared to head out than I did.
As such, I looked at Veyrin’s soul in particular. Eve was already rank 3, and while I might be able to have her reach rank 4, it would cost me dearly. She needed 4000 fusion progress now.

Furthermore, to become a higher-tiered necromancer, I had to collect 10 elite souls and ascend them to rank 3. It seemed smarter to focus on Veyrin and then collect more souls instead of maxing these two out.

I went through the same process as I did with Eve, selecting archers in their stead. The lionkin had a much smaller selection of this archetype, so I had to utilize some of my higher-level Lesser Souls.

Though interestingly, a lot of their lower-level combatants were archers. Perhaps they were the cowards, or the lionkin knew weaklings had a higher chance of being useful if they shot projectiles from range instead of running into the meat grinder that was the enemy armies made up of only veteran soldiers.
These were what remained in my inventory.
(Picture)

Just like Eve, Veyrin had also regained his equipment from the moment of his death and in pristine condition at that. And, just like Eve, he was also still ghostly blue colored. I didn’t know if that would remain their permanent appearance or if they would regain their original colors soon enough...
As Vex was taking her time dressing herself or whatever it was that she found more important than rushing to the aid of the consortium, I did some basic tests with these two.

My findings indicated that they didn’t regain their classes, and they couldn’t speak or non-verbally communicate with me. However, they obeyed my commands perfectly, now seeming a lot more perceptive to detailed instructions as opposed to their rank 1 selves. Furthermore, they were very aware of their surroundings.
When I told them to dodge my punches, they did it masterfully. Their senses were top-notch.

As such, currently, they were high-level soldiers lacking a class and spells. Their immense stats alone made them into respectable combatants, but a similarly statted enemy would likely hold the upper hand. But still. Between level 45 and 50... That was amazing. Most of my girls were in the upper 20s and lower 30s. Even I only hit level 40 thanks to the 10X experience multiplier from Rosie’s gift.

These two will be awesome additions, and by the time I collect the other eight elite souls and become a tier 2 necromancer, I will have the juice to upgrade them further, hopefully giving them their spells back, and perhaps even making them better.

There was another cool discovery I’d made. I could tell them to leave, which would see them dematerialize, their essence traveling back to the [Necrotic Codex]. Casting [Awaken] would let me summon them once again.

Unlike [March of the Damned], where I summoned my Lesser Souls in perfect fighting condition, those that were [Awakened] didn’t have a duration. Lesser souls could only remain summoned for 24 hours, after which they would leave. So it was nice to see that elites could be dismissed as well. I’d been worried they’d be a bit of a nuisance if they were around all the time. This discovery had made them even more convenient than they already were.
Moving on, it was about time I focused on myself for a moment.

With a twitch of my fingers, the water in the air condensed, swirling around me. They twisted through my hair, slicked down my skin, scrubbed gently at the grime, and finally spiraled away, clean. Another motion, and a breeze brushed past my body, drying me in seconds. My clothes materialized from my inventory and fit into place with great comfort. This time, I elected to go for a black tunic, belt, coat, and gloves.
Still, Vex wasn’t done.
Naturally.

I crossed my legs and sat at the edge of the room, letting my fingers drum idly against the armrest of a nearby chair, passing time by inspecting the soul count again and wondering just how fucked the Consortium was.

The 30,000 soldiers they dispatched wasn’t all their power, but the Consortium suffered a heavy blow while the Greenvale family and their many vassals had years to prepare as due to the infighting of the beastkin, they hadn’t had a skirmish in years.
But after what felt like an entire military campaign passing by...
*Click.*
The door opened.
Vex stepped out, a very different woman than the one who’d entered. Gone were the smeared makeup and disheveled hair. In their place stood a confident warrior.

She wore her kendo uniform while her ponytail was gathered high. Over her face, however, sat the Face Shifter—the artifact she used on our way here. I’d since learned its details from her. It was a silvery-white ceramic mask that projected a slightly transformed face. It was how their top agents walked in broad daylight without drawing attention, an expensive Epic-rarity item.

“Next time we’re doing it in your battle attire,” I decreed matter of factly, earning myself a raised eyebrow. She’d clearly entered her Vex the Hexblade persona while changing, so I threw her off with my comment.
Instead of shooting back a flirty response, she just rolled her eyes while smiling.
We began heading up.
At the top of the basement steps, we reached the ground floor of the manor. It was quiet until the shuffle of feet and the clink of a tray reached us.
A young maid rounded the corner, pausing abruptly when she spotted us.
“Lady Verdia?” Her voice held surprise and a note of concern. “You’re leaving already?”
Vex glanced over her shoulder, then sighed. “Yes. We’re going on a business trip. I won’t be back for a while. Keep the mansion tidy in my absence, will you?”
The maid’s shoulders slumped, but she nodded with a small, polite smile. “Understood, my lady.”
She was clearly sad her lady was leaving already. This girl seemed like a maid who was eager to serve Vex.
Vex paused for a moment, sensing the same, but then gave her a small nod and pressed forward.
Outside, we walked for a few minutes until reaching the crowded center, where we slid into a narrow alleyway.

chapters.title: Chapter 788: Goodbyes and Trial Start
paragraphs: I took a breath, raised my hand, and called forth a doorway made up of violet and black. The Warp Gate materialized with its usual hum, casting its light on the cobblestone walls around us.
Vex turned to me. She rose up on her tiptoes and wrapped her arms around my neck, pulling me into a deep kiss. It was soft and slow, and lingered long after it ended.

She whispered, “Good luck on your trial, Quinlan. Come back stronger, but most importantly, just come back to me. It’s ok not to gain another new power... You already have access to so many classes and spells, I can barely wrap my head around them. So don’t stress yourself out. None of us will fault you. Just try your best and whatever happens, happens.”

Her warm words forced a smile onto my face without my permission. I hadn’t expected these words from this eccentric creature. I truly had the best taste in women. They were wild on the battlefield, utterly ruthless against their enemies, uncaring toward strangers, but when it came to those they loved... There were no obstacles that would stop them.
Fierce combatants and even fiercer lovers.
They were all perfect.
Every single one of them.
“Don’t worry your pretty little head about me, Vex. I’ve got this.”

She observed me for a few long seconds, ascertaining I wasn’t trying to hide something from her, until she nodded with a gorgeous smirk, sent a sexy kiss my way, and stepped through the gate, vanishing like moonlight through mist.
I stood there, unmoving. It wasn’t that I lied to her. I just wish we could’ve spent a bit more time together after all we’d been through in recent days.
But all it did was harden my resolve. I had a trial to complete. And nothing would stop me.
I opened a second gate. This one led home.
I stepped through.
I stepped through the gate near the familiar clearing where Rosie’s tree stood tall and proud. The moment I emerged, I blinked in surprise.
Silence.
No elven guards were standing at attention like usual. Rosie was nowhere in sight either.
How strange.
I reached out with my senses, trying to locate the nearest people to me, and then I heard it.
“DADDYYYYYY!!!”
A small blur of green barreled straight toward me like a guided missile.
Before I could brace, Rosie slammed face-first into mine, her little arms wrapping around my head like an octopus made of affection. I stumbled back half a step, chuckling as I peeled her off.
“Still haven’t figured out how to slow down when you do that, huh?”
Rosie beamed at me, her tiny cheeks puffed with pride. “Rosie doesn’t slow down!”
“Oh?” I mused with a smile, ruffling her hair affectionately. “And how did you know that I was here?”

She closed her eyes and raised her chin proudly. “Rosie’s roots travel far and wide under the earth. She can sense everything! Trees, bugs, water, soldiers, portals from which a person giving off such unique signals steps out that Rosie knows he can only be her Daddy—she sees everything!”
Her grin was contagious.
“Impressive,” I said, brushing my knuckles against her cheek. She let out a pleased little squeak, leaning into my touch like a pampered cat.
“Where are your mommies?”
“Mommy Ayame and Auntie Iris dug a hole,” she said innocently.
“...A hole?”
“Mhm! A biiiiiig pit! And they’ve been punching and yelling in it for, like, hours!”
“Hours?”
“Rosie will show Daddy!” she declared, seating herself on my shoulder like a tiny queen. She wrapped her arms around my head for support and began dangling her legs against my chest. “Go that way!”
She pointed dramatically, as if I couldn’t already hear the violent symphony of curses, fists, and cracking bones echoing from the distance.
Still, I humored her, acting like her royal chariot.

We walked together, moving through the outskirts of the stronghold and past the mansion. The sounds of combat grew louder with every step, all the while Rosie was humming merrily as if we were going to watch a fun puppet play instead of a brutal brawl.
Eventually, the terrain shifted. At least the two fierce kittens had the sense in them to move away from the buildings before starting the pummeling. And then we saw it.

A pit. Roughly twenty meters (65 feet) across, crudely carved into the ground like a training arena dug not by Ronan’s professional architect hands but by the two raging ladies who couldn’t wait to throw punches at each other.
Honestly, I was surprised they had the self-control to do this before the brawl began.
... Now that I thought about it some more, it must’ve been the others who forced them to do it.
At the bottom of the pit, two very familiar women could be seen, both looking like they had spent the last few hours inside a blender.

Ayame’s neatly kept, lush hair was undone. Her yukata she liked to wear at home was torn to pieces, and her jaw was red and bruised. Iris’s nose bled freely, and one of her eyes was swollen shut, yet both kept swinging. Neither held their weapons. This wasn’t a duel. This was a grudge match: bare fists, sheer stubbornness, and no ounce of grace left.

Rosie blinked. “Auntie Iris called Mommy Ayame a female goblin among many other colorful names, and said she’d prefer Vex to be the second-in-command. But Mommy Ayame isn’t innocent either. She insulted Iris about having a horrible sense of humor.”
“Haaahhhh...” I sighed, rubbing my temple.
If this was how they acted before Iris officially joined the household, what fresh chaos would blossom once she became a part of it?
“...How am I supposed to make these two friends? Or at least not act like they murdered each other’s loved ones...” I muttered aloud.

“Oh, you’re here already?” Lucille purred from the side. I turned my head and just now realized they’d been having a picnic nearby. “How was your time with Vex? You usually take much longer when you welcome a girl into the harem...”

“She was utterly delicious, a heavenly meal. But sadly, duty called her away rather quickly. Your dearest papa declared war on the Consortium. And thanks to our machinations, the odds aren’t in the syndicate’s favor...”
Upon my statement, her cheeky smile evaporated, replaced by one of surprise. It was Aurora who spoke up next. “Have we been called as well?”
“Nope.”
I heard a sudden feminine giggle, signaling Seraphiel had found something amusing. “Why do I get the sense that you’re planning to sit out the war of your own making...?”

“Sit out? No...” I shook my head, letting an admittedly rather cruel grin. “We’re just... pushing it lower on our list of priorities. I’m about to begin my primordial trial, while I want you girls to spend a bit of time studying your classes in more detail. Once our more pressing matters have been concluded, we’ll see if there are any opportunities to help the Consortium out.”
“Help, he says...” Lucille chuckled amusedly.

“In the dictionary of Quinlan, the word ‘helping my allies’ refers to ‘making opportunistic gains under the veil of supporting my allies.'” Aurora chimed in while nibbling on a snack, sending me a playful wink.
Well, what could I say?
They were all goddamn right.
I wasn’t going to bleed for the Consortium in a losing war, much less risk the lives of my lovers just so that they could continue existing. If the organization was meant to fall here, then so be it.

I’d already gotten immense benefits from them, such as letting me level up under their protection, getting artifacts, and meeting good friends among their ranks and on their missions. But most importantly, my all but secured alliance with Black Fang and her three mighty disciples.
If the worst came to be, I could also just move to dogkin lands and have Papa Vargis assist my future growth. I’m sure he would be delighted to see me back in his palace so soon after saying goodbye.
As such, I allowed myself to focus on what mattered the most: increasing my personal might and the power of the Ascendants, my faction of rapidly rising fighters.
Now, it was time to initiate my Primordial Rank-Up Mission!
[Ding!]
[Primordial Rank-Up Mission initiating!]
